The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- for the accidental injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident took place on 16.01.2023.

2. The Brief facts of the petitioner's case is as under:
It is the case of the petitioner that on 16.01.2023 at about 9.30 a.m., petitioner was riding Scooter bearing Reg. No. MH-49-W- 8607 slowly and cautiously by observing the traffic rules proceeding on Seegehalli-Kadugodi Road,
at that time one Tractor & Trailer bearing Reg. No. KA-07-T-0604 & KA-07-T-0605 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle of petitioner.
Due to which, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately, he was shifted to Axis Hospital wherein he treated as inpatient and petitioner has spent more than Rs.3,50,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance, nourishment, food, transport and other charges.
The petitioner further submitted that, prior to the accident she was heal and healthy and aged about 24 years, the petitioner was working as Software Engineer and earning Rs.35,000/- per month.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has become permanently disabled and lost her future income.
Respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending vehicle and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has filed this petition for a compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- with interest.
3. After service of notice, the respondent No.1 has not appeared before the Court and hence placed exparte.

2
The respondent No.2 appeared through his counsel and filed written statement by denying the contents of the claim petition and also denying the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle.
Further, this respondent admitted the issuance of policy to the offending vehicle and policy was inforce as on the date of accident.
Further, this respondent seeks protection u/s 170, 134(c) and 158(6) of M. V. Act.
He also denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner.
The respondent No.1 further submitted that the driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident.
The petitioner colluding with the owner and police filed the false case.
By these reasons, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

4. On the basis of above pleadings, my learned predecessor framed the following issues are as under:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that on 16-01-2023 at about 9.30 a.m., while she was riding a scooter bearing Reg. No. MH- 49-W-8607 on Seegehalli-Kadugodi road, from Seegehalli towards Kadugodi, slowly and cautiously by observing traffic rules and when she reached infront of Rolla Manrket road, at that time, Tractor and Trailer bearing Reg. No. KA-07-T-0604 and KA-07-T-0605 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger human life and dashed to the petitioner's scooter from behind and caused the accident and due to the forced impact, petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries as alleged by her?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?

3. What order or Award?
5.

In order to prove the case of the petitioner, he has got himself examined as P.W.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to P.21 and examined one Shahid Parveez, Billing Supervisor at Manipal Hospital as PW.2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.22 and Ex.P.23 and examined Anil Ramesh as PW.3 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.24 and 25 and also examined Dr. Deepu N.K as PW.4 and got marked the document at Ex.P26 and closed their side.
On the other hand, respondent No.2 examined its official as RW.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.R1 to Ex.R5.

6. Heard arguments of both the sides and perused the materials placed on record.
7.
My findings on the above issues are as under; Issue No.1: In the affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following:
:REASONS:

ISSUE No.1:

The petitioner has contended that on the above said date, time and place he met with accident and sustained grievous injuries occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of Vaishnavi Sanjay Potdukhe vs Santhosha.R on 15 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124021836/

9.
The petitioner who is injured in this accident has got examined himself as PW-1 by reiterating the averments made in the petition.
He has produced the documents at Ex.P.1 to 21.

Ex.P.1 is the FIR,
Ex.P2 is the complaint, Ex.P.3 is the statement, Ex.P.4 is the spot mahazar, Ex.P.5 is the Sketch,
Ex.P.6 is the IMV Report, Ex.P7 is the Wound certificate, Ex.P8 is the Notice, Ex.P.9 is the Reply Notice, Ex.P.10 is the Charge sheet, Ex.P11 is the Discharge summary, Ex.P.12 is the Notarized copy of Aadhar Card, Ex.P.13 is the Notarized copy of Driving License, Ex.P.14 is the Certificate, Ex.P.15 is the medical bills, Ex.P.16 is the Advance Receipts, Ex.P.17 is the Prescriptions, Ex.P.18 is the Prescription, Ex.P.19 & Ex.P.19(a) & (b) Photos and Pendrive along with certificate u/s 65(b) of Indian Evidence Act, Ex.P.20 is the flight tickets, Ex.P.21 is the Boarding passes.

10. On 16.01.2023 at about 9.30 a.m., petitioner was riding Scooter bearing Reg. No.
MH-49-W-8607 slowly and cautiously by observing the traffic rules proceeding on Seegehalli-Kadugodi Road, at that time one Tractor & Trailer bearing Reg. No. KA-07-T-0604 &
KA-07-T-0605 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle of petitioner.
Due to which, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately, he was shifted to Axis Hospital wherein he treated as inpatient.
Accordingly, the Whitefield Traffic Police have registered a case in Cr.No.10/2023.

After completion of the investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offences punishable U/s 279 and 338 of IPC.
11.
The negligence in common parlance means and simply failure to exercise due care, expected of a reasonable prudent person.
It is a breach of duty and negligence in law ranging from an advertence to shameful disregard of safety of others.
In most instances, it is caused or heedlessness or inadvertence, by which the negligent party is unaware of the results, which may follow from his act.
Negligence is that, a breach of duty or lack of probable care in doing something.
In short, it is want of attention and doing of something, which a prudent and reasonable man would not do.

The burden is upon the petitioner to prove that, the accident occurred due to negligent driving of the driver of the offending Tractor & Trailer bearing Reg. No. KA- 07-T-0604 & KA-07-T-0605.
12.

As we know evidence in any Summary Proceedings, "The act of Negligence" will have to be assessed on the basis of broad preponderance of probabilities and degree of proof required is not one of beyond reasonable doubt, as it is insisted in criminal case for " The Negligent Act ".
13.
The certified copy of the First Information (First information statement/s complaint in common para-lace) lodged before the Whitefield Traffic Police has been marked as Ex.P2.
On receiving the First Information, the Station House Officer chose to register a case in Crime No. 10/2023.

The said certified copy of First Information Report (F.I.R.) is marked as Ex.P1.
14.

During the Course of examination-in-chief, he got marked Ex.P.1 to 10 are the only documents,
which are to be scrutinized to arrive at conclusion- whether the accident was owing to the negligent manner of driving of the driver of offending Tractor & Trailer.

The Ex.P.4 (spot panchanama) and Ex.P.5 (Sketch), clearly discloses the place of accident and that the police, after registering the First Vaishnavi Sanjay Potdukhe vs Santhosha.R on 15 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124021836/
4 Information, held investigation and filed the Ex.P.10, Charge-Sheet against the driver of the offending Car U/s. 279 and 338 of IPC.

sentences.text: The Ex.P.6 i.e., certified copy of the IMV Report discloses that, the accident was not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the vehicle in question.

15. Petitioner/PW.1 in her examination-in-chief she deposed that, on 16.01.2023 at about 9.30 a.m.,
she was riding Scooter bearing Reg. No. MH-49-W-8607 on Seegehalli-Kadugodi Road slowly, when she reached rola market driver of the offending vehicle driven his Tractor in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the scooter from behind and caused the accident.
The learned counsel for respondent No.2 suggested the PW.1 during the cross- examination that, the accident is not caused by the Tractor & Trailer and it is caused by some other vehicle.
But in order to substantiate his version, insurance company has not produced any documents or evidence to show that, accident is not caused by the offending vehicle.

Moreover, after investigation Whitefield traffic police have submitted charge- sheet as per Ex.P.10 against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable u/s 279 and 338 of IPC and other sections of M. V. Act.

So, this itself shows that,
accident is caused due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
16. In support of his case insurance company examined his legal representative as RW.1.
In his examination-in-chief he depose that, the offending vehicle is insured as agricultural tractors under the clause of vehicle in the policy.
The insured was supposed to be used only for agricultural and forestry purpose.

Further he also depose that, as per MLC records maintained by the Axis Hospital,
the alleged accident was taken place due to four wheeler Vs. two wheeler and later it was stroked to Tractor Vs. two-wheeler.
As such, insured Tractor implicated in this case with collusion of petitioner and 1st respondent.

But admittedly, in this case in support of their case insurance company has not produced any document and also they have not challenged the Final report submitted against the driver of the insured vehicle.
Hence, insurance company failed to prove that, accident is not caused due to the driver of the insured vehicle.

17. In a claim of compensation U/s.166 of M.V.Act 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Honble Apex Court in Kusum and others Vs. Satveer and others reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.
18.

sentences.text: In view of the detailed discussion held above, I am of the opinion that, the petitioner has proved negligence on the part of driver of the offending vehicle and as such the accident in question had taken place.

By relying on evidence of P.W.1 and the Police records, I am of the considered view that the accident in question took place due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Tractor &
Trailer bearing Reg. No. KA-07-T-0604 & KA-07-T-0605.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.
19. ISSUE No.2:

The petitioner in his evidence has specifically deposed that, after the accident he was shifted to Axis Hospital, wherein she was given First aid treatment and then shifted to Manipal Hospital, wherein she was admitted as inpatient and took treatment.
Petitioner has stated in the petition that, she is undergoing deep mental shock, severe pain and sufferings.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:

sentences.text: PAIN AND SUFFERING:

In the petition as well as in his evidence PW1 deposed that,
immediately after the accident he was shifted to Axis Hospital, wherein she was given first aid treatment and then shifted to Manipal Hospital, wherein she was admitted as an inpatient from 16.01.2023 to 26.01.2023.
The petitioner has produced the discharge summary marked at Ex.P.11 wherein it is mentioned that the petitioner was admitted in the Manipal Hospital, Bangalore for 10 days.
She has produced the wound certificate marked at Ex.P.7 wound certificate the doctor has opined that the injuries are grievous in nature.
Hence, it is clear that during the above said period the petitioner suffered lot of pain and inconvenience.
Considering all these aspects this tribunal has granted Rs.50,000/- under the head of pain and suffering.
21. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner has pleaded in the petition that she has spent huge amount towards medical expenses.
In support of her plea, she has produced 01 Dental Bill at Ex.P.15 to the tune of Rs.14,500/- and 24 Medical Bills at Ex.P.17 to the tune of Rs.46,005/-.

Further, the petitioner also examined the Billing Supervisor at Manipal Hospital as PW.2, who deposed that,
petitioner took treatment in Manipal Hospital and inpatient bill amount was Rs.5,74,382/- and insurance company has paid Rs.4,62,033/- and remaining amount of Rs.69,459/- is paid by the patient and to prove the same the petitioner has produced the copy of inpatient bills along with advance receipts at Ex.P.16 Advance receipt.
Hence, looking to the injuries sustained and treatment taken by the petitioner.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,29,964/- towards medical expenses.
22. LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID UP PERIOD:

The petitioner has produced Ex.P.11 Discharge summary issued by Manipal Hospital,
Bengaluru, it reveals that, the petitioner took treatment from the said hospital from 16.01.2023 to 26.01.2023 i.e. for 10 days.
Hence, at least 2 months is required to recover from the accidental injuries.

It is the further contended that, the injured petitioner was Software Engineer at MU Sigma Company, ITPL, Bangalore and earning Rs.35,000/- per month, but no reliable evidence is produced by the petitioner to show how much income she was getting from her work.

So, in the absence of any evidence in respect of the income of the petitioner, the petitioner might have monthly income at Rs.16,000/- as per the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka fixed notional income of the year 2023 at Rs.16,000/- per month for determination of income before Lok-Adalat for the Districts coming under the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru Bench.

sentences.text: The accident is of the year is 2023.
Hence, the income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.16,000/-p.m. as per above decision.
Hence, 2 months is to be considered as loss of income.
Hence, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.32,000/- under this head.
23. Towards loss of future earning capacity on account of Permanent Physical Disability-

The petitioner to prove her disability, she has produced the evidence of Dr. Deepu.N.K in order to substantiate the same, PW.4 who has opined that, total disability of right upper limb at 10% and that of whole body disability at 13.33%.
Admittedly, the PW.4 is a treated doctor.

But during the course of cross-examination, the petitioner admitted that, she is still working in MU Sigma business solution Company Pvt. Ltd., as Data Analyst and earning sum of Rs.50,000/- per month, that means the petitioner is continued in service and accidental injuries has not caused any permanent disability.

sentences.text: Hence, petitioner is not entitled for loss of future earning capacity on account of disability.
24. FOOD, CONVEYANCE, NOURISHMENT AND ATTENDANT CHARGES:
Further
the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and took treatment as inpatient in Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru as inpatient from 16.01.2023 to 26.01.2023 i.e., 10 days.

Further, the petitioner submitted that her parents came from Nagpur by flight and spent huge amount for the same and produced the flight tickets and boarding pass which are marked at Ex.P.20 and Ex.P.21, for Rs.28,732/-.

Hence, she is entitled for compensation of Rs.58,732/- under the head of nutritious food, conveyance and attendant charges.
25. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS AS WELL AS MARRIAGE PROSPECTUS :
The petitioner was aged about 24 years at the time of accident, she has sustained grievous injuries.
It shows that she found difficulty in doing day to day works.
She might have suffered lot of pain and loss of amenities and comforts in life.
During the course of argument, learned counsel for petitioner argued that due to injury marriage prospectus of petitioner have been diminished.

Therefore,
considering the age, nature of injuries and percentage of disability, Rs.1,00,000/- is awarded under the head of loss of future amenities and happiness as well as marriage prospectus.
26. TOWARDS FUTURE
MEDICAL EXPENSES :
The petitioner has claimed Rs.6,26,000/- towards future medical expenses.

The doctor who has been examined as PW.4 has suggested future surgeries for Right axillary contracture and estimate of this surgery will be approximately Rs.1,86,000/-,
Breast contracture and estimate of this surgery will be approximately Rs.2,00,000/- and expander removal and multiple advancement flaps and estimate of this surgery will be approximately Rs.2,40,000/-.
By keeping nature of the injuries sustained, as she is bound to suffer medical problems in future and cannot every time depend upon Government hospital.
Hence, under this head Rs.3,00,000/- is awarded.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation under the following heads:
1 Pain and sufferings Rs. 50,000/-
2 Medical expenses Rs. 1,29,964/-
3 Loss of earnings during laid Rs. 32,000/-
up period 4

Nutritious food and Rs. 58,732/-
attendant charges 5 Loss of future amenities and Rs. 1,00,000/-

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.6,70,696/- under various heads.
27. LIABILITY:

As discussed in issue No.1, the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the tractor & trailer bearing Reg. No. KA-07-T-0604 and KA-07-T-0605 and the police have conducted due enquiry and filed charge sheet against the said driver of the offending vehicle.
From perusal of the policy, the offending vehicle was insured with the respondent No.2 for the period from 27.06.2022 to 26.06.2023.
Admittedly, the accident in question took place on 16.01.2023.
Hence, policy was in force at the time of accident.
Though insurance company has taken contention that, owner of the offending vehicle i.e., respondent No.1 violates the terms and conditions of the policy.
They have issued policy towards offending vehicle for the use of agricultural purpose, but he has used the said vehicle for commercial purpose.

Hence, insurance company i.e.,
respondent No.2 is not liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
But in order to support his contention, respondent No.2 has not produced any documents to show that respondent No.1 used the offending vehicle for the commercial purpose.
As such, respondent No.2/insurance company failed to prove that, respondent No.1 violates the terms and conditions of the policy.
Hence, in view of above discussion, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, respondent No.2 being the insurer is liable to indemnify the respondent No.1 owner.
28. INTEREST:

As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, I have relied on a decision reported in M.F.A. No.100090 of 2014 in between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has awarded interest at the rate of 6%.

By relying on the aforesaid decision,
6% interest awarded to the petitioners in the present case on hand.
Accordingly, issue No.2 is answered partly in the affirmative.
29. ISSUE No.3:
In view of above discussions, I proceed to pass the following:
:ORDER:
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of I.M.V Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is awarded with compensation of Rs.6,70,696/- with interest @ 6%
p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- for the accidental injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident took place on 16.01.2023.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has become permanently disabled and lost her future income.
Hence, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Accordingly, the Whitefield Traffic Police have registered a case in Cr.No.10/2023.

11.
The negligence in common parlance means and simply failure to exercise due care, expected of a reasonable prudent person.
It is a breach of duty and negligence in law ranging from an advertence to shameful disregard of safety of others.
In most instances, it is caused or heedlessness or inadvertence, by which the negligent party is unaware of the results, which may follow from his act.
Negligence is that, a breach of duty or lack of probable care in doing something.
In short, it is want of attention and doing of something, which a prudent and reasonable man would not do.
The burden is upon the petitioner to prove that, the accident occurred due to negligent driving of the driver of the offending Tractor & Trailer bearing Reg. No. KA- 07-T-0604 & KA-07-T-0605.
12.
As we know evidence in any Summary Proceedings, "The act of Negligence" will have to be assessed on the basis of broad preponderance of probabilities and degree of proof required is not one of beyond reasonable doubt, as it is insisted in criminal case for " The Negligent Act ".

accident is caused due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
In his examination-in-chief he depose that, the offending vehicle is insured as agricultural tractors under the clause of vehicle in the policy.
Hence, insurance company failed to prove that, accident is not caused due to the driver of the insured vehicle.
17. In a claim of compensation U/s.166 of M.V.Act 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Honble Apex Court in Kusum and others Vs. Satveer and others reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.
18.
From perusal of the policy, the offending vehicle was insured with the respondent No.2 for the period from 27.06.2022 to 26.06.2023.
Hence, policy was in force at the time of accident.
Though insurance company has taken contention that, owner of the offending vehicle i.e., respondent No.1 violates the terms and conditions of the policy.
They have issued policy towards offending vehicle for the use of agricultural purpose, but he has used the said vehicle for commercial purpose.
Hence, insurance company i.e.,
respondent No.2 is not liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
But in order to support his contention, respondent No.2 has not produced any documents to show that respondent No.1 used the offending vehicle for the commercial purpose.
As such, respondent No.2/insurance company failed to prove that, respondent No.1 violates the terms and conditions of the policy.
However, respondent No.2 being the insurer is liable to indemnify the respondent No.1 owner.
As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, I have relied on a decision reported in M.F.A. No.100090 of 2014 in between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has awarded interest at the rate of 6%.

29. ISSUE No.3:
In view of above discussions, I proceed to pass the following:
:ORDER:
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of I.M.V Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is awarded with compensation of Rs.6,70,696/- with interest @ 6%
p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 being insurer of the vehicle involved in an accident is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the above compensation amount with interest thereon before Tribunal within two months from the date of this award.
In the event of deposit of total compensation amount of petitioner, 50% of amount shall be released in his favour along with interest thereon.
Remaining 50% of compensation amount of  petitioner in total compensation amount including interest thereon shall be deposited in his name as F.D. in any of the Nationalized or Scheduled Bank as per choice of petitioner for a period of two years.
After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon, disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA No.
2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated:19.08.2019.
The petitioner is hereby directed to produce particulars of his Bank Account, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contains compulsorily photograph of petitioner, which is duly attested by concerned Bank.
Further petitioner shall produce PAN Card/Adhar Card.
In case of deposit of awarded amount, the petitioner is entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal.
Bank shall not advance loan on such FD, and shall not cause premature release of FD without permission by the Tribunal.
Bank shall release amount along with interest thereon in favour of petitioner after expiry of two years period of deposit on proper verification and identification,
without waiting for further order of court.
The advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
